naics_industry_sector: Health Care and Social Assistance
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase two ambulances for the Gila Regional Medical Center located in Silver City, New Mexico. Both ambulances will be equipped with the necessary medical gear making the units fully operational to provide emergency medical service to the three southwestern counties of New Mexico. The new emergency medical vehicles will replace older ambulances, which are near or past their useful effective service life. The old ambulances have become unreliable due to high usage, and mileage. Because of their age they require constant maintenance making them unreliable which places the publics safety at great risk. The new ambulances will play an important role to quickly give effective emergency medical service which in turn provides a safer community. The service area for the ambulances includes the communities of Bayard, Columbus, Deming, Hurley, Lordsburg, Reserve, Santa Clara, Silver City, and Virden located in Grant, Hidalgo, and Luna counties. This service area is almost 2,000 square miles larger than the states of Delaware Rhode Island combined.

naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
naics_national_industry: OTHER FIRE/RESCUE & PUBLIC SAFETY RELATED SERVICES
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase updated medical equipment. The purchase of the equipment will help Gila Regional Medical Center located in Silver City, New Mexico provide better medical service to the rural residents of this area of the state. The new equipment will include anesthesia machines, ultrasound machines, ventilators, surgical tables, surgical suite lights, a washer for sterile processing, a bipap breathing machine system, a refrigerator, a neo-Vectra-e-stim unit with laser, range, and computers on wheels for documentation at patients bedside. The Gila Regional Medical Center needs the new equipment to replace old and obsolete equipment, which are near or past their useful effective life. Due to the age of the equipment, it is difficult to find parts to repair these pieces of equipment. With the onset of COVID-19, this caused more stress on the already obsolete equipment and in some cases the Medical Center did not have adequate equipment to meet the needs of the hospital. The low reliability of the older equipment places the public safety at great risk. The new equipment plays an important role in the community by enabling the medical center to quickly respond to the needs of its patients. The Gila Regional Medical Center services the communities of Bayard, Columbus, Deming, Hurley, Lordsburg, Reserve, Santa Clara, Silver City, and Virden in Grant, Hidalgo and Luna located in southwest New Mexico.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help the city of Socorro, New Mexico purchase a new street sweeper for its road department. The street sweeper will be used throughout the 14.4 square miles that make up the city. The street sweeper is needed in order to help maintain and control debris and dirt throughout the community. The street sweeping not only makes the streets cleaner, but it is an important part of storm water pollution prevention. It prevents unwanted materials from flowing into the storm drains which could cause backups and flooding. The new street sweeper will also help the city of Socorro look better because dirty streets leave a bad impression on visitors, especially if theyre visiting Socorro for the first time. By keeping the streets of Socorro clean it confirms to visitors the community has pride in itself showing the city is a nice place to live and work.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase two backhoe tractors by the city of Socorro, New Mexico. The backhoes are needed for utility work to maintain gas supply lines and the water and wastewater distribution lines throughout the 14.4 square miles that make up the city of 9,000 people. Specifically, the equipment will be used on an everyday basis to maintain the infrastructure to make sure basic services are provided to the citizens throughout the city. This is especially important to ensure natural gas is delivered without interruption. Also, the equipment will be used to fix water and wastewater line breaks. By doing so the city of Socorro will be protecting drinking water by making sure it is safe and healthy. The city of Socorro qualified for a Persistent Poverty Grant and an Economic Impact Initiative grant from USDA Rural Development because of the citys poverty rate which is estimated at 30.9 percent.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide additional financing to the city of Socorro. They have upgraded and replaced the interceptor sewer lines which were no longer structurally sound. Several lift stations have also been replaced, and additional funding is needed for additives for several roadways that will increase the functionality and operation. The additional funding will pay for a backup generator and concrete pad with the ultimate goal of replacing older sewer lines. This project is a high priority as most of the city of Socorro is served through a centralized gravity sewer collection system. The community has also been identified as a persistent poverty area, with this project serving approximately 9,051 residents in Socorro, N.M.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to refinance debts, working capital, and financing of fees to the owners of the historic Sagebrush Inn in Taos, N.M. When the Inn opened 90 years ago in 1931 it offered 13 guestrooms and quickly became known for its authentic Southwest dcor. Today, the hotel is still known for its southwestern architectural style and now consists of 156 units that offers Wi-Fi, a swimming pool, a spa tub, a restaurant, and laundry services. Over the years numerous celebrities have stayed at the Sagebrush Inn; and movies such as Easy Rider and Twins were shot in and around the hotel. This project will save 100 jobs and will create 50 new jobs.

The KTAO-FM began using solar power to run its transmitter located on top of 10,801 Picuris Peak south of Taos; this was necessary because there is not an electric power line located in the area. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to modify the existing Pueblo of Laguna, Mesita Village east lagoon wastewater system with an additional lagoon cell. The Pueblo of Laguna is in Cibola County in western New Mexico and serves a total of 4,043 tribal residents. The Pueblo of Laguna and the Pueblos Water Utility Authority with assistance from Indian Health Services (IHS), has successfully installed multiple projects over the years with USDA Rural Development financing to repair and rehabilitate the entire wastewater and sewer system for the pueblo. The Mesita Village Lagoon Expansion will be one of those successes when the old and failing septic systems and leach fields are replaced. The current wastewater system is causing a strain on the Utility Authoritys maintenance team and budget, as well as presenting potential health risks to those residents living in Mesita Village. The new lagoon cell will increase evaporation to balance the projected wastewater inflows from the abandoned septic systems and will provide adequate capacity for potential community growth through year 2040. In addition, the project will provide for another 20 years of wastewater treatment and handling for the Mesita Village East community. This project will also bring the system into compliance with health and safety, building and environmental codes.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide funding to allow the Indian Pueblo Cultural Center (IPCC) located in Albuquerque, N.M. to provide technical assistance to give entrepreneurial training to entrepreneurs in the 19 Pueblos across New Mexico. There has been a strong need to provide resources to entrepreneurs for years, as New Mexico and its inhabitants especially the indigenous Native Americans struggle with a challenging economy and the ability to secure gainful employment. The socio-economic challenges faced by those living in the Pueblos extend to the community and in large the region. Pueblo income and job growth also have been anemic over the past five years. The training the Native entrepreneurs will receive will lift them and others economically as they initiate businesses and hire employees to carry out their work. When the entrepreneurial training is completed the IPCC will have provided a mix of online/in-person training for up to 20 Pueblo entrepreneurs. The IPCC estimates 7 part-time jobs and 14 full-time jobs will be created directly from the grant funding.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment was awarded to the Anthony Water & Sanitation District to allow the completion of an expansion of their existing wastewater treatment plant (WWTP). The expansion is needed for WWTP to meet the projected 2036 average flow of 1.3 million gallons per day. To meet this goal the wastewater treatment system will use a parallel circular concentric plant to provide additional capacity and clarification. The expansion will consist of a second circular concentric package plant, identical to the existing unit. This additional wastewater treatment system will allow the District to take the existing WWTP offline for cleaning and rehabilitation before flows increase significantly. The renovation is recommended to prolong the life of the existing structure and equipment. The improvements will address the Districts over capacity issue which results in discharges in excess of the regions total maximum daily load. Which results in the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permit violations. The total amount of loan and grant funding by USDA Rural Development for the construction of this project is $21,119,000. The project will benefit the existing 2,582 residential and 95 commercial users along with the proposed additional 165 residential and 56 commercial users, for a total of 2,747 residents and 151 commercial users that make up the Anthony Water & Sanitation Districts service area.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to pay for the short fall of funding to upgrade the Chamberino Mutual Domestic Water Consumer & Sewer Associations water system. The shortfall was discovered when construction bids were opened. The additional funding will complete the associations water improvement project by including a new 200,000-gallon storage tank and an additional 4,000 linear feet of waterline from the existing tank. The new waterline will provide better pressure and flow to the old part of the service area. The additional financing for this water improvement project was obligated on May 19, 2020 in the amount of a $467,000 grant. This new funding will be used in conjunction with the previously obligated $141,000 loan, and $2,594,200 grant from Rural Development. An additional $435,375 from the State of New Mexicos leverage funding and $2,600 in connection fees were made for this project. The cost for the upgrade to the water system is $3,640,175. The water system upgrade is needed because some of the residents in the Chamberino service area use private water wells, but these wells are going dry and produce poor water quality. However, they are unable to connect to current the system due to insufficient infrastructure that cannot supply water to their homes. Because of this fact this situation has become a health and sanitary issue. This project will alleviate this problem by delivering water with reliable pressure to the community and allow for new connections to be added to the system. The new well and water storage tank will also add a second source of water and storage to the system, which currently only has one water source. The proposed improvements will be used in conjunction with the existing facility to provide safe and reliable drinking water to the community. The project will benefit their existing 219 residential and 6 commercial users.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment was awarded to the Cottonwood Rural Water Association near Artesia, New Mexico for improvements to its water system. The improvements will include upgrading the existing undersized distribution lines for future growth and to provide enough water for fire flow. The funding will also pay for the installation of fire hydrants and will upgrade service meters along the proposed distribution line upgrades. By doing so it will match current water meters in the remaining service area. Funding will also pay for the installation of a mixer at the Firehouse tank that will resolve the stagnant water issue. The money will also be used to acquire approximately 50 acre-feet of water rights that will allow for anticipated growth in the area. Also, the funding will allow the purchase a hydrov machine to allow the Association to locate existing waterlines and other utilities by non-destructive means. This allows the Association to conduct more line repairs and save water loss due to inadvertent line breaks and avoid costly damage to other utilities. This project will address the Associations infrastructure improvements needs, including the lack of backflow devices at the customer service meter, which is a health and sanitary concern by opening the system to potential contamination. Many of these rural services contain livestock watering devices and use pesticides for lawns and gardens that are the basis for the health and sanitary backflow risk. The proposed improvements will be used in conjunction with the existing facility to continue providing safe and reliable drinking water to the community. The project will benefit their existing 608 residential and 23 commercial users. The total amount of funding made by USDA Rural Development for this project is $4,036,000.

By doing so it will match current water meters in the remaining service area. Funding will also pay for the installation of a mixer at the Firehouse tank that will resolve the stagnant water issue. The money will also be used to acquire approximately 50 acre-feet of water rights that will allow for anticipated growth in the area. Also, the funding will allow the purchase a hydrov machine to allow the Association to locate existing waterlines and other utilities by non-destructive means. This allows the Association to conduct more line repairs and save water loss due to inadvertent line breaks and avoid costly damage to other utilities. This project will address the Associations infrastructure improvements needs, including the lack of backflow devices at the customer service meter, which is a health and sanitary concern by opening the system to potential contamination. Many of these rural services contain livestock watering devices and use pesticides for lawns and gardens that are the basis for the health and sanitary backflow risk. The proposed improvements will be used in conjunction with the existing facility to continue providing safe and reliable drinking water to the community. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund the needed water system improvements for the Casa Adobes Mutual Domestic Water Consumers Association located in Mimbres, New Mexico. The funding will also pay for a backup generator for the primary well and install five flush hydrants and two air-release valves. Also, the two remaining deteriorated 10,000-gallon water distribution tanks will be replaced with two new 20,000-gallon welded steel tanks. Other improvement will include the installation of 28 air release valves at high points in the system which will reduce the opportunities for air locking the system. This project will address the Associations Administrative Order issued by the New Mexico Environment Departments Drinking Water Bureau, which resulted due to the Association not addressing the States Sanitary Survey Citations. The proposed improvements will be used in conjunction with the existing facility to provide safe and reliable drinking water to the community.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will result in a Master Development Plan for a 220-acre parcel of land in the heart of the Shiprock, New Mexico located on the Navajo Nation. The project is called River Vision and was selected by the community members through the Rural Development technical assistance program, Rural Economic Development Innovation. The plan is intended to assure adherence to cultural and community values while providing economic and community development and to improve the quality of life for Shiprocks 9,500 residents. Development elements to be addressed in the plan include a 100-room hotel/casino enterprise with restaurants and retail spaces, an RV park, outdoor recreation businesses relating to the adjacent San Juan River. Also, a visitors center with galleries and retail space for Navajo art and crafts will be included in the master plan. In addition the plan will include a museum, a market space for locally produced food products, a community activity center and other compatible business and quality of life opportunities identified during the plan development process. Shiprock is a persistent poverty community and this investment is expected to result in much needed business development and job creation.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development grant investment will be used for the New Mexico Recycling Coalition (NMRC) to provide technical assistance and trainings to rural communities throughout New Mexico. The training is designed to help rural communities to reduce their solid waste stream by focusing on proven methods of sustainable materials management. An introduction and training on Reuse Centers, Back Yard Composting, Fix-It Clinics and Zero Waste activities will empower local communities to divert waste from their landfills while keeping their waterways and landscape clean. Farmers and ranchers within the Edgewood Soil and Water Conservation District service area will benefit from the help provided by Quivira. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to improve and expand the existing wastewater delivery system in Village of Williamsburg, New Mexico. This is a much-needed extensive upgrade of the Villages sewer line delivery system. The sewer system is in bad need of repair and replacement because of issues such as the backup of sewage in the sewer lines in residential neighborhoods. The existing wastewater system was built in the 1940s with a small expansion made in the early 2000s to a section of the Village north of Broadway. None-the-less the Village of Williamsburg applied for the funding because the old sewer lines are failing. There is a concern the deteriorated sewer lines could lead to the leaching of sewage into the groundwater which could make its way to the Rio Grande. When construction is completed the improvements will include; the installation of two 22-KW back-up generators at each lift station location along with other needed equipment. The Riverside and Central Lift Stations will receive much needed repairs to the wet wells and to mend cracks and replace the broken upper portion of the manholes and seal the concrete. Pumps, motors and valves within the dry pit will also be replaced. The new control panels will be installed to run the new motors, local alarm systems, remote terminal units and telemetry equipment. All of which will be compatible with the of City of Truth or Consequences sewer system. The funding will also pay for the replacement of six-inch lines with 3,188 linear feet of 8-inch sewer line and the rehabilitation of 5,671 linear feet of 8-inch sewer line. 240 manholes will be refurbished and the extension of the collection system at the southwest corner of the Village will see 1,000 linear feet of low-pressure sewer lines added with two grinder sewer pumps. The project will benefit the existing 229 residential homes and 17 commercial users.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide additional education to rural first responders through the Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes (ECHO) Program. The weekly education program will better help first responders address the substance abuse disorder in the rural areas of New Mexico. ECHO is a medical education and care management model operated by the University of New Mexico Health Care Sciences Department to teach clinicians how to provide better health care. Project ECHO offers access to specialty health care treatment in rural and underserved areas. This is done through weekly electronic classes. These classes provide front-line clinicians the knowledge and support they need to manage patients with complex conditions. The Rural Community Development Initiative (RCDI) grant provided by Rural Development will utilize the innovative ECHO Model to provide virtual training, technical training, and mentorship to first responders; paramedics, EMTs, police, and fire personnel in rural communities through ECHOs video teleconferencing system. The financing through the RCDI grant will increase the first responders knowledge base and teach them methods and best practices for responding to substance abuse and overdose calls in their communities.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to rehabilitate old existing sewer to lines at the Pueblo of Laguna which is a federally recognized Native American Tribe located 46 miles west of Albuquerque, New Mexico. The Pueblo is comprised of six district jurisdictions. The financial support will also see the connection of sewer services to homes that currently dont have sewer services. This project will focus on three of the Pueblos villages including; the Village of Paraje that is the home to 829 residents, the Village of Laguna which has 986 residents and the Village of Mesita that has a population of 832 residents. The funding will also pay for the enlargement of the Mesita sewage lagoon. By doing so the sewage capacity will be increased which will address future growth of the service area. When completed the project will solve health and sanitary and possible environmental issues by eliminating the use of the old existing sewer lines.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to expand and build a vacuum sewer collection service to the San Ysidro colonia and surrounding area located north of Las Cruces, New Mexico. The project includes construction of a new gravity and vacuum wastewater collection system and 55,000 feet of sewer lines. A vacuum sewer system is a method of transporting sewage with air pressure from its source to a sewage treatment plant. This type of sewer system is needed for this project because of the high water table in the area. The new sewer lines will be placed in shallow trenches because of the close proximity of the water table. Once completed the new vacuum sewer lines will route the wastewater to existing wastewater lines which flow to the City of Las Cruces wastewater collection system and treatment facility. The construction of this wastewater delivery system is badly needed because the 569 homes and three businesses that will be connected to the sewer lines are currently using cesspools or septic tanks. Ultimately, with this new system the environmental concern of ground water contamination will be eliminated. Once the design for the system is completed and approved, it is expected to take eight months to complete construction of the wastewater system with construction expected to begin in the early part of 2021. The combination of funding used for this project is part of USDAs Waste and Environmental Programs Persistent Poverty loan and grant program, as well as the Colonias grant program.

project_name: South Valley Water Supply & Treatment Project
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: Rural Development funds will upgrade and modernize the Berino, New Mexico water system. The financing package made to the Lower Rio Grande Public Water Works Authority for the $4,966,400 project includes a $323,335 Colonia Grant. The combined funding will pay to drill a new water well within 100 feet of the old existing well and the installation of an arsenic treatment facility and a new storage tank. The expanded water service will create a redundant water supply source for the residents of Berino. This is being done in case the nearby Mesquite and Desert Sands water systems are not able to provide enough water as a back-up service to the Berino water system in an emergency. When completed the updated water system will also address the arsenic concentrations in the groundwater in the Berino area and provide cleaner water to the residents of Berino. The improvements will benefit the 874 residential users and 16 commercial users currently serviced by the Berino water system.

The financing package made to the Lower Rio Grande Public Water Works Authority will pay to drill a new water well within 100 feet of the old existing well and the installation of an arsenic treatment facility and a new storage tank. The expanded water service will create a redundant water supply source for the residents of Berino. This is being done in case the nearby Mesquite and Desert Sands water systems are not able to provide enough water as a back-up service to the Berino water system in an emergency. When completed the updated water system will also address the arsenic concentrations in the groundwater in the Berino area and provide cleaner water to the residents of Berino. The improvements will benefit the 874 residential users and 16 commercial users currently serviced by the Berino water system.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to implement the Local Innovators Institute (LOI), a restaurant accelerator . LOI is a business accelerator organization dedicated to help small restaurant owners reduce their financial risk when opening a new restaurant. LOI provides information and workshops outlining the fundamentals in owning and managing a restaurant through hands on experience, --as well as testing the consumer palate. LOI focuses on three business fundamentals: restaurant knowledge, business basics and branding/marketing. As a part of the accelerator, the individual participants will be given the opportunity to sell from a food truck a few times per week at LOIs present location. This allows the participants an opportunity to pitch their restaurant and food service concept and share items from their menu with the public. This project will take place in Lovington, New Mexico located Lea County in southeast New Mexico. This project is especially important because it supports the development of small and emerging private business enterprises in the rural areas of Lea County.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to support technical assistance given by Sandoval County staff and contractors to small and emerging businesses. The technical assistance will be in the form of a yearlong business support process in four rural Sandoval County communities. The support will provide guidance to individual businesses, especially in the tourism industry. Specialists will implement small business development education ground-tested by the Albuquerque Small Business Resources Collaborative. This technical assistance is being implemented because of a regional economic development plan that highlights rural areas caught in the shadow of our large urban core (Albuquerque). The four rural New Mexico communities in Sandoval County being targeted for this technical assistance because of the urban influence include; Jemez Springs, Jemez Pueblo (Native American), Tijeras, and Cedar Crest. Extremely skilled and experienced staff in tourism and business will provide the training. At least six businesses will receive the assistance with three jobs expected to be created with five more saved.

project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used to fund a WEP grant for Tesuque Pueblo in the amount of $1,613,017. The funding for this project will be used to rebuild the waste water treatment plant in Tesuque, NM. This new facility is a necessity as the old system needed upgrade and expansion as many rural homes within the planning area currently use individual on-site wastewater treatment and dispersal systems. The wastewater from these homes enters the septic tank where solids settle out and the effluent is sent to a drain field. The solids that accumulate in the septic tanks are emptied by a septic tank pumping service as needed. This is costly for the residents and the individual septic tanks are failing, which puts a high risk for ground water contamination. This project will serve approximately 700 residents in the community of Tesuque Pueblo, NM. Other funding sources includes $800,000 from the State of New Mexico and $330,000 from Tribal Infrastructure Funds, as well as a previous USDA RD pre-planning grant in the amount of $30,000 for a total project cost of $2,773,017.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to have a broadband study completed in Sierra County, New Mexico to identify the current broadband infrastructure, identify gaps in service areas, and identify infrastructure needs to provide better broadband services to county-wide businesses and users. Sierra County is a rural community with limited to no broadband services. In order to stimulate economic development and retain existing businesses, a broadband study is crucial for Sierra County to determine the best way to move forward for implementing broadband services. Broadband is an economic development priority for the county and identified in the countys economic development plan. The local economy is varied: agriculture, ranching, health care, mining, hunting and outfitting, tourism, and recreation. All of these industries require high speed broadband services to function. The project will help move Sierra County closer toward updated broadband services, which in the next three years, five jobs will be created and ten more jobs will be saved. It will also allow existing businesses to operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and work at full capacity. For example, it will prevent patients from having to be transferred from Sierra Vista Hospital to other facilities outside the region. Currently the hospital is losing patients and revenue due to lack of reliable internet and broadband services.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used replace and rehabilitate the waterline and wastewater system upgrades in Truth or Consequences, New Mexico. The upgrade will include the replacement of the existing gas chlorination system, and the installation of Variable Frequency Drives (VFD) on existing booster water pumps. A VFD is a device used to provide better control and increase productivity on the pumps. The funding will also pay for equipment that measures the flow of the water and to inject chlorine in the water delivery system. A new backup generator at the Citys Cook Street Water System Facility will also be installed. The project will also provide necessary upgrades to the existing wastewater treatment plant which includes necessary upgrades to the drinking water Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition/ Human Machine Interface (SCADA) system which is a computer system that monitors and controls the water delivery to the Citys customers. When done the project will see the replacement of approximately 32,800 feet of old and leaking lines in the downtown area of Truth or Consequences. The replacement of the old water lines is vital because the new water lines will reduce water losses, and increase the overall water system efficiency, and alleviate a health and sanitary issue. The project will benefit 2,460 residential, 477 commercial users, 53 city and 3 industrial users along with the neighboring Village of Williamsburgs 243 residential and 22 commercial users.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to develop a Preliminary Engineering Report (PER) and an environmental document for the Village of Williamsburg, N.M. proposed wastewater system improvements project. The PER is necessary to establish the need for a wastewater project in this community of 720 residents. The reports must meet certain criteria. For example; the PER must meet the RUS Bulletin 1780-2 guide which outlines the projects scope and improvements for the proposed wastewater improvement project. As for the environmental document the report will have to meet the requirements of 7 CFR 1970 which is the federal governments environmental policies and procedures. RD funds will be used in conjunction with the Village of Williamsburgs $39,815 contribution to complete both reports. These reports will enable the Village of Williamsburg to submit another application to Rural Development for funds to design and construct the Villages wastewater system improvements.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development grant investment will be used to purchase 2 police vehicles for the City of Socorro. The need for new vehicles is due to their current vehicle fleet having aged with high mileage and needs constant repairs. The low reliability of these older vehicles places the public safety at great risk. The City of Socorro police department need for reliable vehicles and equipment is essential. The new police vehicles play an important role in the community to provide quick response, to solve criminal activities and provide a safe community where the citizens can live, work or socialize. The service area coverage typically includes the city boundaries. Based on the 2010 census, these vehicles will serve a rural area with a population of 9,059 that are located in the Persistent Poverty county of Socorro. The Median Household Income (MHI) of the area is $32,057, which is 80% below the State Nonmetropolitan MHI of $43,797. Therefore, the City of Socorro was eligible for Community Facility Persistent Poverty grant funds of up to 35%.
